title: Traditions
lead: Traditions are the seventh of the seven ideas, and they cover what is handed on from one generation to the next.

p: A tradition is a custom, belief or practice passed between generations. It can create continuity and group identity, while adapting over time.
In plain words, a tradition is a way of doing things that older people have handed on to younger people.

writers.name: Functionalists
writers.says: emphasise how traditions can create a shared identity and sense of belonging.

list: Morris dancing in England keeps features such as bells, sticks and handkerchiefs that connect it to earlier performances.
A family might continue celebrating Eid or Diwali while taking part in other local celebrations.
Sharing a family recipe with younger relatives may help to pass a tradition to another generation.
A present-day community festival can retain established dances while sharing performances online, so the tradition continues while some things change.
A school carol service held every December keeps readings and hymns that earlier generations of pupils heard, while a video now lets relatives who cannot attend watch it.
Relatives who live abroad joining a long-standing family Christmas or Eid meal by video call are keeping the tradition going in a new way.

p: Define the term: A tradition is a custom, belief or practice passed between generations. It can create continuity and group identity, while adapting over time.
Item link: The bells and handkerchiefs in the item connect current Morris dancing to earlier performances, making the tradition recognisable.

quote.t: Morris dancing continues in England. Dancers retain features such as bells, sticks and handkerchiefs, but may perform with their own musicians or in different venues, including pubs.
